questions.stem: A 14-month-old boy has had eczema on his face and arms since he was 3 months old. He has had four ear infections and one pneumonia. His parents have seen streaks of blood in his stools and small red spots on his legs. His mother's brother died at age 5 from bleeding in the brain. Laboratory studies show a platelet count of 28,000/µL (normal 150,000-400,000) and a mean platelet volume of 5.1 fL (normal 7.5-11.5). Serum IgM is low, IgA and IgE are high, and IgG is normal. The blood smear shows few, very small platelets. The defective protein most likely has which normal function?
choices: Signaling from the pre-B cell receptor for B-cell maturation
Binding of platelets to von Willebrand factor through glycoprotein Ib
Making superoxide during the phagocyte respiratory burst
Remodeling the actin cytoskeleton in blood cells
Activating B cells and macrophages through CD40 on their surface
questions.explanation: Eczema, recurrent infections and **thrombocytopenia with small platelets** in a boy with an X-linked family history mean **Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome**. The **WAS protein** links receptor signals to the **actin cytoskeleton** in blood cells, so T cells, platelets and other leukocytes work poorly. Bernard-Soulier syndrome (glycoprotein Ib defect) also causes bleeding with a low platelet count, but its platelets are **large**, and it causes neither eczema nor infections.
questions.explanation_pt: Eczema, infecções recorrentes e **plaquetopenia com plaquetas pequenas** em um menino com história familiar ligada ao X indicam **síndrome de Wiskott-Aldrich**. A **proteína WAS** liga os sinais dos receptores ao **citoesqueleto de actina** nas células do sangue, então linfócitos T, plaquetas e outros leucócitos funcionam mal. A síndrome de Bernard-Soulier (defeito da glicoproteína Ib) também causa sangramento com plaquetas baixas, mas as plaquetas são **grandes** e ela não causa eczema nem infecções.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman has had sinusitis or pneumonia several times a year for 5 years. A chest CT shows bronchiectasis. Last year she had chronic watery diarrhea, and stool tests found Giardia. She also has immune thrombocytopenia. An HIV test is negative, and she takes no immunosuppressive drugs. Serum albumin is normal, and there is no protein in her urine. Laboratory studies show IgG 180 mg/dL (normal 700-1,600), IgA 12 mg/dL (normal 70-400) and IgM 20 mg/dL (normal 40-230). Flow cytometry shows normal numbers of CD19+ B cells and CD3+ T cells. Antibody levels do not rise after tetanus and pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccines. Which process is most likely defective?
choices: Maturation of pre-B cells into mature B cells in the bone marrow
Differentiation of B cells into antibody-secreting plasma cells
Class switching from IgM to other isotypes in germinal centers
Transport of dimeric IgA across the mucosal epithelium
Positive selection of developing T cells in the thymus
questions.explanation: Adult-onset sinopulmonary infections, *Giardia*, autoimmunity, **low IgG, IgA and IgM**, poor vaccine responses and **normal B-cell numbers** fit **common variable immunodeficiency (CVID)**: B cells are present but do not become **plasma cells**. Normal albumin and no proteinuria argue against antibody loss through the gut or kidney. X-linked agammaglobulinemia also lowers all antibodies, but it blocks maturation in the bone marrow, so **B cells are absent**, and it presents in infant boys. A class-switch defect (hyper-IgM syndrome) would leave IgM normal or high.
questions.explanation_pt: Infecções sinopulmonares de início na vida adulta, *Giardia*, autoimunidade, **IgG, IgA e IgM baixas**, resposta vacinal fraca e **número normal de linfócitos B** indicam **imunodeficiência comum variável (IDCV)**: os linfócitos B estão presentes, mas não se tornam **plasmócitos**. Albumina normal e ausência de proteinúria falam contra perda de anticorpos pelo intestino ou pelo rim. A agamaglobulinemia ligada ao X também reduz todos os anticorpos, mas bloqueia a maturação na medula óssea, então os **linfócitos B estão ausentes**, e ela surge em meninos lactentes. Um defeito de troca de classe (síndrome de hiper-IgM) deixaria a IgM normal ou alta.

questions.stem: A 5-week-old girl is brought in because her umbilical cord stump is still attached. The skin around the umbilicus is red, swollen and firm, but there is no pus. Her parents are first cousins. Temperature is 38.4°C. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 46,000/µL with 85% neutrophils; hemoglobin and platelet count are normal, and her blood type is A, Rh-positive. A swab of the umbilical area grows Staphylococcus aureus. Which step of neutrophil function is most likely defective?
choices: Rolling on endothelium through selectin binding
Killing of ingested bacteria with reactive oxygen species
Fusion of phagosomes with lysosomes
Movement toward C5a and IL-8 in the tissue
Firm adhesion to endothelium through β2 integrins
questions.explanation: **Delayed cord separation**, omphalitis **without pus** and a very high blood neutrophil count fit **leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1**: loss of **CD18** stops neutrophils from binding **ICAM-1** firmly, so they stay in the blood and cannot reach the tissue. LAD type 2 blocks the earlier **rolling** step (missing sialyl Lewis X), but it also causes the Bombay blood group, so her red cells would type as group O, not group A. In chronic granulomatous disease, neutrophils reach the tissue and form pus, and the neutrophil count is not this high.
questions.explanation_pt: **Queda tardia do coto umbilical**, onfalite **sem pus** e neutrofilia muito alta no sangue indicam **deficiência de adesão leucocitária tipo 1**: a perda do **CD18** impede que os neutrófilos se liguem firmemente à **ICAM-1**, então eles ficam no sangue e não chegam ao tecido. A LAD tipo 2 bloqueia a etapa anterior de **rolamento** (falta de sialil Lewis X), mas também causa o fenótipo Bombay, então as hemácias seriam tipadas como grupo O, não grupo A. Na doença granulomatosa crônica, os neutrófilos chegam ao tecido e formam pus, e a contagem de neutrófilos não fica tão alta.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl has had many boils on her neck and back since early childhood. The abscesses are large, but they are not warm, red or painful. She has had two pneumonias caused by Staphylococcus aureus, each followed by thin-walled air cysts in the lung. She has had eczema since infancy, and she broke her arm after a minor fall. Her primary teeth have not fallen out, and her permanent teeth are growing in behind them. Laboratory studies show eosinophils at 12% of leukocytes and a serum IgE far above the normal range. Which immune response is most likely deficient?
choices: Differentiation of Th17 cells that recruit neutrophils
Production of superoxide by phagocyte NADPH oxidase
Lysis of bacteria by the membrane attack complex
Firm adhesion of neutrophils to vascular endothelium
Killing of intracellular microbes by IFN-γ-activated macrophages
questions.explanation: "Cold" staphylococcal abscesses, lung cysts (pneumatoceles), eczema, fractures after minor trauma, **retained primary teeth** and **very high IgE** mean autosomal dominant **hyper-IgE (Job) syndrome**. A **STAT3** defect blocks **Th17** differentiation, so little IL-17 is made and neutrophils are poorly called to the infected tissue. Chronic granulomatous disease also causes staphylococcal abscesses, but the abscesses are inflamed, other catalase-positive organisms such as *Serratia* and *Burkholderia cepacia* appear, and retained teeth and high IgE are not features.
questions.explanation_pt: Abscessos estafilocócicos "frios", cistos pulmonares (pneumatoceles), eczema, fraturas após traumas leves, **retenção dos dentes decíduos** e **IgE muito alta** indicam **síndrome de hiper-IgE (Job)** autossômica dominante. Um defeito de **STAT3** bloqueia a diferenciação **Th17**, então pouca IL-17 é produzida e os neutrófilos são mal recrutados para o tecido infectado. A doença granulomatosa crônica também causa abscessos estafilocócicos, mas eles são inflamados, surgem outros organismos catalase-positivos como *Serratia* e *Burkholderia cepacia*, e retenção dentária e IgE alta não fazem parte do quadro.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old girl has had three ear infections and one episode of bronchiolitis since age 5 months. She is growing and developing normally. Laboratory studies show IgG 140 mg/dL (normal for age about 220-900), with IgA and IgM slightly low. Flow cytometry shows normal numbers of CD19+ B cells. Her antibody levels against tetanus and Haemophilus influenzae type b rose normally after her routine vaccines. Which best explains her low IgG?
choices: Absent maturation of pre-B cells because of a BTK defect
Loss of IgG through the intestine
Slow start of her own IgG production after maternal IgG has fallen
Defective CD40 ligand on helper T cells that blocks class switching
Failure of B cells to become plasma cells throughout life
questions.explanation: **Maternal IgG** crosses the placenta and falls by about 6 months. In **transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy** the child's own IgG production starts late, so IgG stays low for months, but **B cells are normal** and **vaccine responses are normal**; levels usually recover by early childhood. X-linked agammaglobulinemia is the most tempting answer, but B cells would be absent, vaccine responses would be absent, and it affects boys. CVID does not start this early, and its vaccine responses are poor.
questions.explanation_pt: A **IgG materna** atravessa a placenta e cai até cerca dos 6 meses. Na **hipogamaglobulinemia transitória da infância**, a produção da própria IgG começa tarde, então a IgG fica baixa por meses, mas os **linfócitos B são normais** e a **resposta vacinal é normal**; os níveis costumam se normalizar no início da infância. A agamaglobulinemia ligada ao X é a resposta mais tentadora, mas os linfócitos B estariam ausentes, a resposta vacinal também, e ela afeta meninos. A IDCV não começa tão cedo, e a resposta às vacinas é fraca.

questions.stem: A 3-month-old girl has oral thrush that keeps coming back and a chronic cough. In her first week of life she had seizures caused by low serum calcium, and she had surgery for an interrupted aortic arch. Flow cytometry shows very few CD3+ T cells and normal numbers of CD19+ B cells. If one of her lymph nodes were examined, which region would most likely be depleted of lymphocytes?
choices: Primary follicles of the cortex
Paracortex (deep cortex)
Medullary cords
Medullary sinuses
Subcapsular sinus
questions.explanation: Neonatal **hypocalcemia**, a **conotruncal/aortic arch** heart defect and very few T cells point to **DiGeorge syndrome** (22q11.2 deletion): the **third and fourth pharyngeal pouches** fail to form the thymus and parathyroid glands. The **paracortex** is the **T-cell zone** of the lymph node, so it is poorly populated. The cortical follicles are the **B-cell zone**; they are depleted in X-linked agammaglobulinemia, not here, where B cells are normal.
questions.explanation_pt: **Hipocalcemia** neonatal, cardiopatia **conotruncal/do arco aórtico** e pouquíssimos linfócitos T indicam **síndrome de DiGeorge** (deleção 22q11.2): a **terceira e a quarta bolsas faríngeas** não formam o timo e as paratireoides. O **paracórtex** é a **zona de linfócitos T** do linfonodo, então fica pouco povoado. Os folículos corticais são a **zona de linfócitos B**; eles ficam depletados na agamaglobulinemia ligada ao X, não aqui, onde os linfócitos B são normais.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old girl has had chronic diarrhea and poor weight gain since she was 6 weeks old, and oral candidiasis returns after each course of nystatin. She received BCG at birth; the vaccination site on her right arm is now a growing ulcer, with enlarged lymph nodes in the right axilla. Her parents are first cousins, and an older brother died of an infection at 5 months of age. Chest x-ray shows no thymic shadow. Flow cytometry results: CD3+ T cells 40/µL (very low), CD19+ B cells 5/µL (very low), CD16/CD56+ NK cells 600/µL (normal for age). Adenosine deaminase activity in her red cells is normal. Which process is most likely defective?
choices: Signaling through the common γ chain of cytokine receptors
Removal of toxic deoxyadenosine from developing lymphocytes
Formation of the thymus from the third pharyngeal pouch
Signaling from the pre-B cell receptor through BTK
Joining of gene segments to build antigen receptors
questions.explanation: Infant diarrhea, failure to thrive, recurrent thrush, a spreading **BCG infection** and **no thymic shadow** mean **SCID**. The profile **T−, B−, NK+** with autosomal recessive inheritance points to **RAG1/RAG2** deficiency: **V(D)J recombination** is needed to build both T-cell and B-cell receptors, while NK cells do not rearrange their receptor genes. A **common γ chain** defect is the most common SCID, but it is X-linked, NK cells are absent and B cells are present. ADA deficiency also lowers T and B cells, but NK cells are low too and ADA activity would be low.
questions.explanation_pt: Diarreia, baixo ganho de peso, candidíase oral recorrente, **infecção disseminada pelo BCG** e **ausência da sombra tímica** em um lactente indicam **SCID**. O perfil **T−, B−, NK+** com herança autossômica recessiva aponta para deficiência de **RAG1/RAG2**: a **recombinação V(D)J** é necessária para formar os receptores dos linfócitos T e B, enquanto as células NK não rearranjam os genes de seus receptores. O defeito da **cadeia γ comum** é a SCID mais comum, mas é ligado ao X, as células NK estão ausentes e os linfócitos B estão presentes. A deficiência de ADA também reduz linfócitos T e B, mas as células NK também ficam baixas e a atividade de ADA estaria baixa.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy has X-linked chronic granulomatous disease. Genetic testing found a mutation in CYBB, the gene for the gp91phox subunit of NADPH oxidase. His 30-year-old mother has never had a serious infection. Her neutrophils are tested with dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry after stimulation. Which result is most likely?
choices: Two groups: one with normal fluorescence and one with none
One group with normal fluorescence in all cells
One group with no fluorescence in any cell
One group with about half of normal fluorescence in all cells
Two groups: one with normal and one with half-normal fluorescence
questions.explanation: Because of **random X inactivation (lyonization)**, each neutrophil of a female carrier uses either the normal or the mutant **CYBB** allele. So the DHR test shows **two populations**: cells with a normal respiratory burst and cells with none. The idea of uniform half-normal fluorescence is wrong because no single cell expresses both alleles. Carriers usually stay healthy because enough normal cells remain, unless inactivation is strongly skewed toward the mutant X.
questions.explanation_pt: Por causa da **inativação aleatória do X (lyonização)**, cada neutrófilo de uma portadora usa o alelo normal ou o alelo mutado de **CYBB**. Assim, o teste da DHR mostra **duas populações**: células com explosão respiratória normal e células sem nenhuma. A ideia de fluorescência uniforme pela metade está errada, porque nenhuma célula expressa os dois alelos. As portadoras costumam ser saudáveis porque restam células normais suficientes, a menos que a inativação seja muito desviada para o X mutado.
